note: Treaty of Bassein 1802 (Baji Rao II and the English): primary chapter HIS-16. This chapter ends its Maratha narrative at the First Anglo-Maratha War (1775-1782); no fetched NCERT/IGNOU source used here covers the 1802 treaty.

First Maratha War during Warren Hastings' tenure: primary chapter HIS-16. The war itself (1775-1782, Maratha victory) IS taught in section panipat_aftermath from the NCERT Class VIII timeline, but Warren Hastings' tenure is not covered by any fetched source, so the keyed answer cannot be derived from this chapter.
Ranjit Singh, leader of the Sukerchakia misl: BHIC-134 Unit 2 (Sukerchakias held Gujranwala, Wazirabad; Ranjit Singh son of Sukerchakia chief Mahan Singh). Also a practice question (q10).

Council of Barabhais organised by Nana Phadnavis: none of the fetched sources (NCERT VII ch.10, NCERT VIII ch.3, IGNOU BHIC-110 Unit 1, BHIC-134 Unit 2) mentions Nana Phadnavis or the Barabhai council. Left untaught rather than written from memory.

'Haindava-Dharmoddharak' title of Shivaji: Shivaji's coronation (1674, Raigad) is taught in section shivaji, but the title itself appears in none of the fetched sources. Left untaught rather than asserted without a quote.

Khalsa founded by Guru Gobind Singh (1699): primary chapter HIS-12, but taught here too — NCERT VII ch.10 places the institution of the Khalsa in 1699 in Guru Gobind Singh's career. Also practice question q09.

Farrukh Siyar's 1717 farman to the East India Company: primary chapter HIS-16. Farrukh Siyar appears in this chapter only as a later Mughal emperor (assassinated 1719) and as Asaf Jah's patron; the 1717 farman is not in any fetched source used here.
Third Battle of Panipat fought in 1761: taught from IGNOU BHIC-110 Unit 1 (battle commenced 14 January 1761). Also practice question q08.
First independent Nawab of Bengal, Murshid Quli Khan: taught from NCERT VII ch.10 and IGNOU BHIC-110 Unit 1 (governor 1717, link with Delhi limited to tribute). Also practice question q04.
